title: API Rate Limit
seoTitle: What Is an API Rate Limit? Plain Guide for Business
seoDescription: What API rate limits are, why integrations with Shopify, WhatsApp or Zoho hit them, and how well-built integrations queue and retry safely.
summary: An API rate limit is the maximum number of requests a service allows in a period of time. When an integration sends too many requests, for example during a bulk stock sync, the service temporarily refuses them. Well-built integrations queue requests and retry, so nothing is lost.

dataPoints.label: Where you meet them
dataPoints.value: Shopify, WhatsApp Business API, Zoho, Google APIs, payment gateways

dataPoints.label: Typical symptom
dataPoints.value: Syncs that work for ten records but fail for ten thousand

dataPoints.label: Correct handling
dataPoints.value: Queues, back-off and retry, batching, and alerting on persistent failures

dataPoints.label: Wrong handling
dataPoints.value: Ignoring errors, leaving records silently unsynced

body:
## Why it matters

An order sync that silently drops records during a sale is worse than one that is slow. Ask any integration partner how they handle rate limits and failures, and whether you get alerted.

See our entries on [APIs](/glossary/api), [webhooks](/glossary/webhook) and [integration](/glossary/integration).

faqs.q: Can we pay for higher limits?
faqs.a: Some providers offer higher limits on bigger plans; good design usually matters more.

faqs.q: Do no-code tools handle rate limits?
faqs.a: Partly; at high volume, custom queuing is often more reliable.
